title: Canonical augmented strict integral completion and normalized open strict comparison data
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and schemes in a universe $t$ independent of the field universe $u$. Use the completed module categories $\mathcal M_T$, strict towers, standard derived categories, actual quotient-complex functor $F_T$ and universal derived reduction pair $(Q_T,\epsilon_T)$ of [def-a1-integral-completed-tower-pullback-universes]. Let $\Delta_T$ be the constant strict-tower functor and $L_T=R\lim$ the total right derived functor of ordinary inverse limit, with its derived adjunction $\Delta_T\dashv L_T$ and its actual comparison on complex representatives [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Use the Grothendieck structure at module size $\max(u,t+1)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]. Define the normalized augmentation $\gamma_T:\Delta_T\to Q_T$ by the following determining property: on every flat-term K-flat representative $P$, there is one strict chain map $a:\Delta_TP\to F_TP$, whose degree-$i$, level-$n$ component is the recorded quotient unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and $\gamma_T(QP)\epsilon_T(P)$ equals $Q(a)$ composed with the exact constant-functor computation isomorphism. Choose this uniquely determined natural transformation. Define $C_T=Q_TL_T$ and $\eta_{T,H}$ to be the derived constant-tower adjunction unit followed by $L_T(\gamma_{T,H})$. On the actual shifted-cone Roos functor, define signed coordinates by its recorded biproduct isomorphism, swapping the factors and negating the second, so the differential is $(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$. Define the ordinary-limit-to-Roos map by the compatible family of limit projections.
For an open immersion $e:V\hookrightarrow W$ and a pinned coefficient/operation presentation $o$ [def-sf-integral-open-operations], use exact ringed-slice restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], its termwise complex and strict-tower functors and their exact derived localizations. Define its constant-tower comparison by the identity on constant diagrams, and the section-transport map by the coefficient equivalence counit. Define $\alpha_H$ to be the target constant-tower adjunction unit followed by $R\lim$ of the pulled quotient augmentation, using that constant comparison. Define the graph into the chosen base change by the pair of the identity and the structure map. Finally define strict comparison assertion data to consist of finite and completed coefficient isomorphism properties, quotient-transition compatibility, preservation of flat-term K-flat representatives, a natural isomorphism $e^*F_W\simeq F_Ve^*$ normalized on every local pure tensor, strict transition and actual strict augmentation squares, its derived strict-tower isomorphism, and its good-representative computation-counit and augmentation equations. This record asserts no existence of a comparison. All quotient indices $n\in\mathbf N$ denote exponent $n+1$.

proof.text: In each degree assemble the recorded unrestrictedTowerUnit maps into a morphism of strict towers. Consecutive naturality is the quotient transition formula on 1 tensor x, since the coefficient transition preserves one. NatTrans.ofOpSequence supplies naturality for all arrows. The existing chain maps supply differential compatibility, and scalar-extension adjunction-unit naturality supplies naturality in the input complex.

Compose the exact constant-functor computation isomorphism with the derived image of this ordinary natural transformation. Apply Mathlib Functor.leftDerivedLift to the universal counit of reductionPair. Its leftDerived_fac_app identity is exactly the augmentation normalization; the strict map has the stipulated components by construction.

For uniqueness, use the proved localization of flat-term K-flat representatives from IntegralOperationsWellDefined. On each good representative, the component formula determines the strict chain map by degreewise and levelwise extensionality. Both normalized derived maps therefore have the same composite with the reduction counit. This counit is invertible on good representatives, so cancellation gives equality there. Localization.natTrans_ext gives equality of the natural transformations on the full derived category. The remaining definitions and instances retain their original constructions.
